name: Filled Red Waterskin
summary: In Tarren Mill, a well gives clear spring water for a shaman’s trial. The Filled Red Waterskin bears water drawn from the village well, amid ruins held by the Forsaken.

sections.title: A Beacon in Blighted Lands
sections.body:
Brine sends shaman initiates from her hermitage in the Barrens to Tarren Mill to train with water. The journey leads into the Hillsbrad Foothills, where decay and the dead surround the town. Yet the well at its heart still gives clear spring water.

To Brine, that pure water endures as a sign of life in an unhallowed land. She likens the spring, untouched by corruption, to Warchief Thrall’s resolve through hardship. Gathering the water tests whether an initiate honors its purity, even in hostile surroundings.

faq.q: What is inside the Filled Red Waterskin?
faq.answer: The Filled Red Waterskin holds pure spring water drawn from the public well at the center of Tarren Mill.

faq.q: Why does Brine want water from Tarren Mill?
faq.answer: Brine sees Tarren Mill’s fresh spring as a rare sign of purity amid Forsaken decay. She needs the water to brew sapta for a shaman’s water trials.

faq.q: How does the well stay clean in an undead town?
faq.answer: No one knows why the spring has stayed untouched by the plague around it. Brine says the Forsaken in Tarren Mill may not recognize or value the purity of the holy spring among them.

faq.q: How does Thrall relate to this quest?
faq.answer: Brine compares the clean well in a ruined town to Thrall. He endured great suffering and captivity, then emerged strong and untainted to guide the orcish people through dark times.

angles.text: As a shaman, carrying this water tests your ability to find and honor life-giving balance in the world’s most decayed and sorrowful corners.
As a Horde champion from Kalimdor, you travel to Tarren Mill, where the Forsaken struggle against Alliance forces across the Eastern Kingdoms.
